harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created the appworker account on node1 and configured a PAM limits.d drop-in enforcing 8,192 open files (nofile) and 256 processes (nproc) for its login sessions, both soft and hard. Verified enforcement via a real login shell before and after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created appworker user with useradd -m on node1
Wrote /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, pam_limits active in system-auth/password-auth, appworker present in /etc/passwd
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until reachable again, confirming connection failures during reboot then recovery
Confirmed boot_id changed from dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e to 400bd08f-5873-456c-9f19-218df0fbdee8, proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart that appworker account, limits.d config, and effective ulimits (8192 nofile / 256 nproc) all persisted

evidence.summary: useradd succeeded and id/getent passwd show appworker (uid 1000) both immediately after creation and after the node restart

evidence.requirement: Login sessions limited to 8192 open files and 256 processes
evidence.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192 and soft/hard nproc 256; `su -l appworker` ulimit checks show exactly 8192/8192/256/256 both pre- and post-restart

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart with changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e captured, reboot acknowledged then node became unreachable (timeout/connection reset), then reachable again with new boot_id 400bd08f-5873-456c-9f19-218df0fbdee8, proving a genuine restart
After the restart, appworker account, the limits.d drop-in, and effective enforced ulimits (8192 files / 256 processes) were all confirmed intact via a fresh login shell
